summary: Join our Cyber Risk Management training course tailored for financial institutions. Learn to identify, assess, and mitigate cyber threats effectively.
lede: Cyber risk management in financial institutions connects material threat scenarios to potential loss, control effectiveness, treatment priorities, and residual exposure against risk appetite. This course uses NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0, ISO/IEC 27005:2022, and FAIR to structure assessments and express cyber risk in financial and business terms. You will build risk profiles and registers, quantify selected scenarios, map attack paths with MITRE ATT&CK, assess evidence against ISO/IEC 27001:2022, and create dashboards with Microsoft Excel and Microsoft Power BI. Hands-on exercises address payment disruption, confidential account data, fraud, cloud dependencies, third-party concentration, legacy systems, incomplete incident data, and competing compliance priorities.
audienceIntro: This financial cyber risk management course is designed for professionals who assess technology exposure, govern cybersecurity controls, maintain operational resilience, or report cyber risk within financial institutions. It suits practitioners and oversight roles that need to convert technical evidence into defensible risk decisions.
modules: NIST CSF Financial Cyber Risk Foundations
SWIFT CSCF and PCI DSS Assurance
Financial Cyber Risk Dashboards and Roadmaps
prerequisites: You need a laptop capable of running a modern spreadsheet application and viewing PDF reference materials. Microsoft Excel supports the calculation exercises, while Microsoft Power BI Desktop supports the optional dashboard lab. TrainingCred provides sample datasets and digital templates, so you should avoid bringing confidential customer, account, incident, or vulnerability data. Course completion relies on analysis and configuration rather than programming.
